947	  /**
948	   * Update user permissions from external JSON
949	   *
950	   * @param {Object} absPermissions JSON containing user permissions
951	   * @returns {Promise<boolean>} true if updates were made
952	   */
953	  async updatePermissionsFromExternalJSON(absPermissions) {
954	    if (!this.permissions) this.permissions = {}
955	    let hasUpdates = false
956	
957	    // Map the boolean permissions from absPermissions
958	    Object.keys(absPermissions).forEach((absKey) => {
959	      const userPermKey = User.permissionMapping[absKey]
960	      if (!userPermKey) {
961	        throw new Error(`Unexpected permission property: ${absKey}`)
962	      }
963	
964	      if (!['librariesAccessible', 'itemTagsSelected'].includes(userPermKey)) {
965	        if (this.permissions[userPermKey] !== !!absPermissions[absKey]) {
966	          this.permissions[userPermKey] = !!absPermissions[absKey]
967	          hasUpdates = true
968	        }
969	      }
970	    })
971	
972	    // Handle allowedLibraries
973	    const librariesAccessible = this.permissions.librariesAccessible || []
974	    if (this.permissions.accessAllLibraries) {
975	      if (librariesAccessible.length) {
976	        this.permissions.librariesAccessible = []
977	        hasUpdates = true
978	      }
979	    } else if (absPermissions.allowedLibraries?.length && absPermissions.allowedLibraries.join(',') !== librariesAccessible.join(',')) {
980	      if (absPermissions.allowedLibraries.some((lid) => typeof lid !== 'string')) {
981	        throw new Error('Invalid permission property "allowedLibraries", expecting array of strings')
982	      }
983	      this.permissions.librariesAccessible = absPermissions.allowedLibraries
984	      hasUpdates = true
985	    }
986	
987	    // Handle allowedTags
988	    const itemTagsSelected = this.permissions.itemTagsSelected || []
989	    if (this.permissions.accessAllTags) {
990	      if (itemTagsSelected.length) {
991	        this.permissions.itemTagsSelected = []
992	        hasUpdates = true
993	      }
994	    } else if (absPermissions.allowedTags?.length && absPermissions.allowedTags.join(',') !== itemTagsSelected.join(',')) {
995	      if (absPermissions.allowedTags.some((tag) => typeof tag !== 'string')) {
996	        throw new Error('Invalid permission property "allowedTags", expecting array of strings')
997	      }
998	      this.permissions.itemTagsSelected = absPermissions.allowedTags
999	      hasUpdates = true
1000	    }
1001	
1002	    if (hasUpdates) {
1003	      this.changed('permissions', true)
1004	      await this.save()
1005	    }
1006	
1007	    return hasUpdates
1008	  }

## Wave 2 report: User is SKIPPED (sent 16:57)

The nested single include objects are confirmed on the real file with the real check, and under your reading of rule 5 they have no fix. User.js is fully restored; nothing of mine is left in the repo.

### The blocker, exact errors (check finished 16:52:45, first-pass User.ts)
```
server/models/User.ts(842,15): error TS2769: No overload matches this call.
  Overload 1 of 2, '(this: ModelStatic<PodcastEpisode>, identifier: Identifier, options: Omit<NonNullFindOptions<any>, "where">): Promise<...>', gave the following error.
    Object literal may only specify known properties, and 'model' does not exist in type 'Includeable[]'.
  Overload 2 of 2, '(this: ModelStatic<PodcastEpisode>, identifier?: Identifier | undefined, options?: Omit<FindOptions<any>, "where"> | undefined): Promise<...>', gave the following error.
    Object literal may only specify known properties, and 'model' does not exist in type 'Includeable[]'.

  Overload 1 of 2, '(this: ModelStatic<Model<any, any>>, identifier: Identifier, options: Omit<NonNullFindOptions<any>, "where">): Promise<...>', gave the following error.
    Type '{ model: sequelize.ModelCtor<sequelize.Model<any, any>>; attributes: string[]; required: false; include: { model: typeof MediaProgress; where: { userId: string; }; required: false; }; }' is not assignable to type 'Includeable | Includeable[] | undefined'.
      Types of property 'include' are incompatible.
        Object literal may only specify known properties, and 'model' does not exist in type 'Includeable[]'.
  Overload 2 of 2, '(this: ModelStatic<Model<any, any>>, identifier?: Identifier | undefined, options?: Omit<FindOptions<any>, "where"> | undefined): Promise<...>', gave the following error.
    (same three lines as overload 1)
```
- User.ts 842 is User.js:748 (the nested include at 747-750). User.ts 866 is User.js:772 (the nested include at 771-775). The first-pass file was 94 lines longer at that point.
- Why there is no fix: both are arguments to Sequelize's `findByPk`. Sequelize types a nested `include` as an array only (node_modules/sequelize/types/model.d.ts:705). A cast on the argument and a hand-written registry signature are the two things you ruled out, and no annotation makes an object literal assignable to an array type.

### The other predicted blockers: all confirmed, each has a fix inside the rules
The fixes were not applied, so they are not verified.

| User.js line | Error on the real file | Fix inside the rules |
|---|---|---|
| 762 | `(856,38) TS2339: Property 'mediaProgresses' does not exist on type 'PodcastEpisode'.` | annotate the const as `PodcastEpisode & { mediaProgresses?: MediaProgress[] }` |
| 784, 792, 793 | `TS2339: Property 'mediaType' / 'media' does not exist on type 'Model<any, any>'.` (libraryItem entry left vague, as you said) | single-step cast on the returned row |
| 678 | `(772,85) TS2339: Property 'metadata' does not exist on type 'BookExpanded \| PodcastExpanded'.` | structural parameter annotation |
| 634, 635 | `TS2790: The operand of a 'delete' operator must be optional.` | explicit interface for `json` |
| 798 | `(892,7) TS2322: Type '(MediaProgress \| null \| undefined)[]' is not assignable to type 'MediaProgress[]'.` and `(892,74) TS18049: 'mediaProgress' is possibly 'null' or 'undefined'.` | two `!` (assigned on the line above) |
| 819 | `(913,9) TS2322: Type 'string \| Date' is not assignable to type 'string \| null'.` | annotate the payload object |
| 959, 965, 966 | `TS7053` (permissionMapping indexed by a string; UserPermissions indexed by a key) | index signature on the permissions data interface; `Record<string, string>` on the static |

Two more that I had not predicted, both fixable by annotation:
- User.js:536: `(630,22) TS2339: Property 'type' does not exist on type 'Model<any, any>'.` The `beforeDestroy(user)` hook in init() gets a plain Model, so its parameter needs `user: User`.
- User.js:152, 154, 156: `TS7053 ... can't be used to index type '{}'` on the reduce accumulator in getSampleAbsPermissions(). It needs a type argument on reduce.

First-pass artefacts, not blockers:
